classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. The operation definitions and three-set example distinguish membership in all three sets from membership in A and either other set.

content.prompt:
True or False? Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets in a universal set $U$.

$(A\cap B)\cap C=A\cap(B\cup C)$.

answer.worked:
False. The left side requires membership in all three sets; the right requires membership in $A$ and at least one of $B$ or $C$. For $U=\{1\}$, $A=B=\{1\}$ and $C=\varnothing$,
$$\begin{align*}(A\cap B)\cap C&=\varnothing,\\A\cap(B\cup C)&=\{1\}.\end{align*}$$
